potential multiple preventive maintenance tasks on ma-

windows. Ziaee (2014) designed an eficient heuristic al-

ably good solutions very quickly that can be embedded

considered unavailability periods on machines with fixed
interval. They solved this problem with a dual-ants colony
algorithm. Jing et al. (2017) studied probability based-
preventive maintenance. In this problem, they consider
a probability of machine failure and process a preventive
maintenance if the probability reaches a specific threshold.
They solved this problem with a multi-objective GA. In
a more recent study, Wang et al. (2021) considered both
preventive maintenance and transportation process with
energy consumption. They used a multi-objective evolu-

Besides the aforementioned works, the FJSSP-nfa has not
seen much interest, which can partially be explained by the
lack of benchmark instances. Indeed, all the works used a
limited number of instances (less than 10) which does not
allow a clear and fair comparison between approaches.
Most studies with maintenance constraints considered
heuristic and meta-heuristic approaches. The eficiency of
current days solvers (such as IBM CPLEX) and the lack
of exact approaches led us to consider a MIP solution
method to close the gap in the literature. Exact solution
approaches can reach optimality on some instances which
is valuable to evaluate the performance of non-exact meth-
ods such as meta-heuristics in later studies. To the best of
our knowledge, no MIP model has been proposed in the
literature for the FJSSP-nfa. Our first contribution is to
propose a novel MIP formulation for the FJSSP-nfa. To
evaluate the performance of our method we faced the lack
of publicly available benchmarks for this problem with
only a few instances from Gao et al. (2006) and Wang
and Yu (2010). Our second contribution is to propose a
large benchmark for the problem, generated from classical
FJSSP benchmarks. The proposed benchmark is both di
verse in terms of instance size and maintenance location on
the horizon. A result comparison is performed to evaluate
our approach and the impact of maintenance tasks in the
scheduling process.

interval. They solved this problem with a dual-ants colony
algorithm. Jing et al. (2017) studied probability based-
preventive maintenance. In this problem, they consider
a probability of machine failure and process a preventive
maintenance if the probability reaches a specific threshold.
They solved this problem with a multi-objective GA. In
a more recent study, Wang et al. (2021) considered both
preventive maintenance and transportation process with
energy consumption. They used a multi-objective evolu-
tionary algorithm as a solution approach.
Besides the aforementioned works, the FJSSP-nfa has not
seen much interest, which can partially be explained by the
lack of benchmark instances. Indeed, all the works used a
limited number of instances (less than 10) which does not
allow a clear and fair comparison between approaches.
Most studies with maintenance constraints considered
heuristic and meta-heuristic approaches. The eficiency of
current days solvers (such as IBM CPLEX) and the lack
of exact approaches led us to consider a MIP solution
method to close the gap in the literature. Exact solution
approaches can reach optimality on some instances which
is valuable to evaluate the performance of non-exact meth-
ods such as meta-heuristics in later studies. To the best of
our knowledge, no MIP model has been proposed in the
literature for the FJSSP-nfa. Our first contribution is to
propose a novel MIP formulation for the FJSSP-nfa. To
evaluate the performance of our method we faced the lack
of publicly available benchmarks for this problem with
only a few instances from Gao et al. (2006) and Wang
and Yu (2010). Our second contribution is to propose a
large benchmark for the problem, generated from classical
FJSSP benchmarks. The proposed benchmark is both di
verse in terms of instance size and maintenance location on
the horizon. A result comparison is performed to evaluate
our approach and the impact of maintenance tasks in the
scheduling process.

4. CONCLUSION
In this study, we considered a flexible job shop scheduling
problem under availability constraints. A MIP model has
been proposed to solve the FJSSP-nfa. In order to test
the proposed model, we introduced the first large bench
mark for this problem and solved it. The experimental
results shows the efectiveness of the model on small- and
medium-sized instances.
As future research, we consider multiple perspectives. The
solving process can be enhanced by designing good lower
bounds or valid inequalities. Constraint programming is
also a promising perspective with the recent works in this
field.

4. CONCLUSION
In this study, we considered a flexible job shop scheduling
problem under availability constraints. A MIP model has
been proposed to solve the FJSSP-nfa. In order to test
the proposed model, we introduced the first large bench
mark for this problem and solved it. The experimental
results shows the efectiveness of the model on small- and
medium-sized instances.
As future research, we consider multiple perspectives. The
solving process can be enhanced by designing good lower
bounds or valid inequalities. Constraint programming is
also a promising perspective with the recent works in this
field.
